[[1966 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] | first_round = | fewnum = 15 | fewest = [[1966 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] | mostnum = 25 | most = [[1966 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] | overall = 305 | rounds = 20 | hofnum = {{ Collapsible list | title = 2 | 1 = OT [[Tom Mack]] | 2 = CB [[Emmitt Thomas]] }} | prev = [[1965 NFL draft|1965]] | next = [[1967 NFL/AFL draft|1967]] }} The '''1966 NFL draft''' was held at the [[569 Lexington Avenue|Summit Hotel]] in [[New York City]] on Saturday, November 27, 1965.{{cite web |url=http://www.profootballhof.com/history/story.jsp?story_id=1998|title=1966 NFL Draft|access-date=September 27, 2008 |publisher=Pro Football Hall of Fame}}{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=NLtOAAAAIBAJ&sjid=XQEEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7229%2C4865273 |newspaper=Toledo Blade |location=Ohio |agency=Associated Press |title=Nobis, Grabowski top picks as pros tap college talent|date=November 28, 1965 |page=3E }} The expansion [[1966 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] were awarded the first pick in each round as well as the final pick in each of the first five rounds. The [[List of first overall National Football League Draft picks|first overall selection]] was [[Tommy Nobis]], a [[linebacker]] from [[1965 Texas Longhorns football team|Texas]]. The league also provided the Falcons with an [[1966 NFL expansion draft|expansion draft]] six weeks later. This was the last draft in which the NFL and the [[American Football League|AFL]] selected their players separate of one another. As a result, most players drafted by teams from both leagues chose to play for the more established NFL, but not all. Similar to [[1965 NFL draft|1965]], the [[1966 American Football League draft|AFL draft]] was held on the same day. After the [[AFL–NFL merger|merger agreement]] in June 1966, a common draft was held in March [[1967 NFL/AFL draft|1967]]. ==Player selections== {| |- |style="background-color:#FFCC00; border:1px solid
